US 10-year yield falls below 5% as investors flock to safe havens
article:
(Oct 23): US Treasuries surged — sending the US 10-year yield back below 5% — as investors sought shelter from tumbling share prices for companies leading the boom in spending on artificial intelligence (AI).

The rally trimmed yields across maturities by as much as 13 basis points (bps), with five- to 30-year yields reaching their lowest levels in nearly a month. In addition to haven demand, Treasuries benefitted from fading expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rates hikes next year.

With doubts about the sustainability of US economic growth if AI investment falters, investors flocked to bonds despite resurgent oil prices. Global benchmark Brent crude oil futures topped US$112 a barrel for the first time since May after deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened concerns that escalating Middle East hostilities could hit supply.

“It’s really encouraging for rates that Treasuries are behaving like a safe haven asset despite the higher oil price on the day,” said Michael Chang, interest-rate derivatives strategist at Citigroup Inc.

Stock-market declines have revived the haven status of US government debt in recent weeks. Previously, the oil-driven inflation resurgence since the US started a war with Iran in late February had driven yields to multi-year highs in anticipation of additional Fed rate hikes to contain it.

See also: Indonesia eyes panda bond in November as it confronts MSCI risk — Bloomberg

Shares of US semiconductor companies — a proxy for sentiment around AI investments — resumed falling on Thursday, sending the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down as much as 6.3% to its lowest level since late July.

The path forward for the world’s largest government bond market may depend in part on whether elevated oil prices or worries about the AI stock trade gain the upper hand.

“Sentiment seems to be shakier these days as investors reconsider AI-related assets,” said Eugene Leow, senior rates strategist at DBS Bank Ltd. “With US yields still elevated by recent standards, investors may want to hedge off some of these risks by seeking safety in Treasuries.”

See also: Long-term Treasuries hold gains as oil snaps three-day rally

“Today’s price action highlights haven demand will overwhelm any worries about inflation and the Fed, if risk assets sour further. Given the higher coupon buffer to cushion total returns and still uncertain backdrop for the AI trade, bonds now hold more appeal,” says Tatiana Darie, macro strategist, Markets Live at Bloomberg Strategists.

Treasuries also benefitted along with German government bonds from the ongoing selloff in French debt. French yields across maturities reached multiyear highs, with the 10-year topping 5.14% for the first time since 2002, and they exceeded German counterparts by historically wide margins.

Despite retreating from session highs, the France’s 10-year yield exceeded Germany’s by more than 170bps, the most since 2011, when the euro debt crisis was at a fever pitch and speculation was mounting that the European Union could break apart. French financial assets have been hit by mounting investor anxiety about its debt burden and the eruption of cost-of-living protests.

The US bond rally trimmed the expected yield for an auction of five-year Treasury inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, at 1pm New York time. The auction was still poised to draw the highest yield for a five-year TIPS auction since October 2023.

A Bloomberg gauge of returns on Treasuries has climbed about 1.2% in October after rounding off its biggest monthly drop in almost two years in September.

“Even though oil has been slowly rallying, Treasuries have been feeling some safe-haven flows again,” said Kenneth Crompton, head of rates strategy at National Australia Bank.

title: US stocks drop as risk-off views dominate with oil up, Meta falling
article:
(Oct 22): US stocks declined Thursday as escalating concern about Mideast conflict pushed oil prices higher, spurring inflation fears with US midterm elections less than two weeks away. Meta Platforms Inc tumbled as investors parsed its results along with the rest of the latest batch of technology earnings for evidence that massive spending on artificial intelligence (AI) is paying off.

Tech shares led the broader stock market lower, with the Nasdaq 100 Index sliding 2.4% as of 11.19am in New York. The S&P 500 Index fell 1.3%, while West Texas Intermediate crude rose 1.1% to US$98.18 a barrel. Yields on 10-year Treasuries retreated to 5%. The US ordered some diplomats and their families out of Saudi Arabia because of the threat from Houthi militants, and at least four people were killed by attacks on an Aramco oil site and a Saudi Arabian airport on Wednesday.

“Investors should stay invested for further equity gains via broadly diversified exposure across sectors and regions,” while building resilience via fixed income and commodities, Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, UBS global equities head said in a note.

Meta slid 5.9% even after reporting better-than-expected results and boosting its capital spending outlook. Shares had initially traded higher following the results, as CEO Mark Zuckerberg touted its AI agent Muse. On Thursday, a gauge of the company’s credit risk surged to a fresh record as spending plans reignited fears tech giants will issue more debt in an already-saturated market. Tesla Inc shares shed 0.78% after the electric-car maker cut its spending plans. Elevated operating expenses underscored the cost of its AI, robotics and autonomy push.

The sector faces broad threats, according to Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok. “If the AI payoff is slow to materialise or never arrives, venture capital returns would come under pressure, since the capital funding today’s token spending would have little to show for it, and a pullback in venture funding could in turn weaken demand for compute,” he warned in a note.

See also: Berkshire stock hits new high, moving on from Buffett’s exit

Chipmakers and other tech stocks fell after reports from Tesla, Lam Research Corp and IBM underwhelmed, weighing on growth sectors and pushing cryptocurrency-linked names lower. Lam Research’s weaker-than-expected guidance weighed on the broader chip-equipment complex, overshadowing a beat from Texas Instruments Inc. Apple Inc rose 0.2%.

If losses in technology stocks hold until the close, the Nasdaq 100 will post its worst day since June. The tech-heavy index is eyeing a fourth day of a move of at least 1% in either direction in five sessions.

See also: Nasdaq 100 climbs as SpaceX results fuel AI trade

Developments in Europe also spurred unease, as French bond stress deepened with investors ditching riskier assets around the world. “German bunds and US Treasuries are the flight to safety trade in the face of this, for now,” Peter Boockvar, author of The Boock Report, wrote in a note. He expects that “at least in the short term, yields in the US have seen a temporary peak.”
• Financials and real estate, as Blackstone Inc reported assets under management and real-estate assets under management that fell short of estimates.
• Airlines, after American Airlines Group Inc forecast a wider-than-anticipated quarterly loss per share and said it expects higher fuel expenses. On Wednesday, United Airlines Holdings Inc forecast weaker-than-expected earnings, underscoring how soaring jet fuel prices are eating into airline profits despite resilient demand for travel.
• Homebuilders, after PulteGroup Inc missed estimates, with chief executive officer Ryan Marshall saying that “the rapid increase in interest rates has stretched affordability even further, made selling an existing home even harder, and has pushed even more consumers to the sidelines.”
• Retreating yields on 10-year Treasuries, which are linked with mortgage rates, may offer some support for real estate companies.
• Consumer staples, after better-than-expected results from bellwether Procter & Gamble Co, along with appetite for defensive names after lackluster tech reports.
• Memory stocks, with broader weakness in AI-linked companies. Western Digital Corp is expected to report earnings after the close.
• Crypto stocks, as Bitcoin drops below US$82,000 on AI jitters.
